data.reason: I follow the LLM's recommendation and stay at v2 (block_k 2). Option 1 improves on-time on 5/5 seeds: on-time 219.4 to 222.8 (+3.4), late 3.4 to 0.0, p95_wait_s 93.2 to 56.8, blocked s 1217 to 121, lowest on-time rate 0.96 to 1.00. These are real service gains, but small. Service is already high under v2 (lowest on-time rate 0.96, unfinished 0.0). The costs are large. C's utility would fall from 46.9 to 21.4, more than half of it. Road violations, whose safety meaning is unknown, would rise from 34.8 to 40.0. They have already grown from 28.0, the level I accepted in D2 for one period on the condition that I would reconsider if they persisted or grew. They have grown, so relaxing blocking further now would contradict that condition. The D2 bar for overriding the companies was consistent multi-period customer gains. For block_k 2 to 1 there is only this one period's measurement. The votes are A for, B for, C against, and I do not know whether the vote passes under the quorum rule. Even if it passes, I do not adopt it now: customers are not the only stakeholders whose safety may be at stake, and the gain of +3.4 orders does not outweigh a 54% loss to one company plus rising violations of unknown meaning. Keeping v2 means customers continue to bear about 3.4 late deliveries per period and a p95 wait of 93.2 s instead of 56.8 s. I accept this known cost for now. I am not rejecting further blocking relief permanently, but the violation trend under v2 must be addressed first. This decision does not settle D2.f2 (revert to block_k 3 or not); it stays open for period 4.
assumptions: Road violations may carry a real safety cost even though their meaning is unknown.
Next period's measurements under v2 will be comparable to this period's.

Whether the vote on option 1 passes under the current quorum rule.
Whether the +3.4 gain of block_k 1 would persist in other periods and other demand.
How C would respond to losing more than half its utility.
Whether reverting to block_k 3 or another rule would cut violations and C's loss at an acceptable customer cost.
How customers perceive the remaining 3.4 late deliveries and the 93.2 s p95 wait.
